2026-10-13 performance: spec 019 in work, slices perf-ws-compression, perf-presence-batch, perf-incremental-check and perf-metrics-under-load approved at G3 (PR 141, 142, 143, 145). Presence leaves at most once in 50 ms with the first frame at once: a plain 50 ms tick doubled the gaps against the web app's own 50 ms. The check of a 1000-element board went from 62 to 4 ms on a laptop; a ring of parents no longer makes the repair depend on element order. Owner chose a port of its own for metrics (TIKO_METRICS_PORT): a request on port 8000 crosses the event loop whatever the route does. Nothing measured on the reference host yet: that is slice perf-remeasure. Next: perf-workers, starting with the plan T050; with several processes each has its own counters, so metrics are touched again.

2026-10-13 workers: slice perf-workers approved at G3. Owner's decisions on the plan T050: the proxy picks the process of a board, the guest socket's contract changes, limiters go to SQLite instead of pinning requests to one process, a metrics port per process. TIKO_WORKERS processes on consecutive ports; a board's room lives in the process named by the last two hex digits of its id, nginx and the API share the rule. Sign-out and role changes are told over Unix sockets, a REST save is passed to the board's process. A guest must not learn the board's id (an existing test says so), so the socket path ends with a two-character room key. Every transaction is BEGIN IMMEDIATE now: reads of different processes wait for each other, to be measured in perf-remeasure. Not tried: several ports of a private service on Render, the guest page in a real browser. Next: perf-remeasure, ask the owner before spending on droplets.

2026-10-13 landing: owner asked for a landing page at tiko.run in place of the redirect to the guide and approved the structure (G1): a static Astro site in site/ on Cloudflare Pages, the hero as a board drawn in DOM and CSS that plays a scene, no animation library, scenarios instead of customer stories, GitHub as a link without a star count, tiko Cloud as "Coming soon" with no e-mail form. Spec 020, slice landing approved at G3 after the owner's look at the local preview (PR 147). The site serves the installers and redirects the guide's paths itself. Left: T009 the checks on the Pages address, T010 pointing tiko.run at it; an e-mail list for tiko Cloud needs a privacy policy and is a slice of its own.

2026-10-13 remeasure: slice perf-remeasure, results in specs/019-performance/results.md, approved at G3. Rooms of 30 on boards of 1000 elements: one core holds 4 and 5 at the edge (the baseline held 1), four cores with TIKO_WORKERS=4 hold 20; past the limit nobody is dropped. nginx takes 16 to 20% of the host at the heaviest passing step, so P7 is asked for. Many small rooms: 200 pass and 500 sit at the limit on one core, and that row is noise of a shared vCPU, the baseline's 78 ms did not come back on its own code. With more cores the next limit for many single visitors is the database, not the CPU. BEGIN IMMEDIATE between processes cost under 3 ms in rooms. Owner on 2026-10-13: P7 goes ahead, and what this run found becomes a new spec, the second round of performance.

2026-10-13 G1 and G2 performance 2: owner approved spec 021 as drafted. Slices R0 to R8 in the drafted order: trusted runs first, then the database under many single visitors, the cost of a scrape, the socket path (019's P7), edits in the room's tick, a save that writes what changed, presence at 10 Hz only if the remeasure asks, the remeasure, the verdict. The verdict names, by measured triggers, whether SQLite, the socket layer, Python in the room or the proxy is the limit; replacing any of them is a spec of its own. The reference run is on DigitalOcean again, with a third target of 8 cores. Next: slice perf2-measure.

2026-10-13 performance 2: slice perf2-measure approved at G3 (PR 155). tiko_db_held_seconds tells the time the database is held by the kind of work, named after the storage method that asked. scripts/load/repeat.py runs a step several times or against several builds in turn and prints the median with the least and the most, the CPU of each container for the window from its cgroup, and the server's side. Checked on a throwaway local stack; the switch between two real images was not tried, only the taking of turns. A visitor's address may start only a few demos, so every run of visitors.py takes new addresses. Next: slice perf2-db-readers.

2026-10-13 performance 2: slice perf2-db-readers approved at G3 (PR 156). Requests that only read have a connection of their own and take no write lock; 25 storage methods moved to it. The transaction that grew with the data was the list of a person's boards: an OR over two conditions made SQLite read every board. On a laptop with 4400 people in the database the wait for the database went from 1.22 to 0.04 ms. Migration 014 adds an index for the sweep of expired sessions. Not measured cleanly: 500 visitors at once, that run crossed the limit of demo visitors. Owner on 2026-10-13: making room for a visitor at the limit is fixed now as a small slice of its own, perf2-demo-room, before perf2-metrics-cost.

2026-10-13 performance 2: slice perf2-demo-room approved at G3 (PR 157). Opening a board over the live socket stored its first live state as a save with a new version, so a demo visitor who only looked counted as one who changed something: a week instead of an hour, and no place given up when the demo was full. The first live state is now stored without a new version (keep_live_state). The search for an idle visitor starts where the last one ended; that place is a hint, and the demo is called full only after a search from the start. On a laptop, 3000 visitors at a limit of 3000 and 300 newcomers: none let in before, all after. The public demo runs released images, so it gets this with the next release; its two demo visitors were removed by hand at the owner's request, with a copy of the database made first. Next: slice perf2-metrics-cost.

2026-10-13 performance 2: slice perf2-metrics-cost approved at G3 (PR 158), no code. A scrape every 5 s against none, 400 visitors on a laptop, three runs each in turn: the API container at 21.7% and 22.0% of a core, every latency inside the spread; one scrape answers in 3 ms. Owner on 2026-10-13: an ok for all of it, go on through the slices. The agent reads that as G3 given ahead for the slices of spec 021 that build what the spec says; a choice the spec leaves to the owner (the direct socket of R3, anything that changes the install or the contract) still stops. Next: slice perf2-socket-path.

2026-10-13 performance 2: slice perf2-socket-path merged under the owner's ok for the slices of spec 021 (PR 159). TIKO_SOCKET_DIR, off by default: each API process also listens on a Unix socket in a directory shared with the web container, and nginx reaches it there. On a laptop, three rooms of 30: about a tenth less CPU in both containers, the ranges touch. Whether the compose files turn it on, and the host's network (T031), wait for the reference run. Found before building perf2-edit-batch: of 643 to 650 messages a second a room sent in spec 019, 600 were presence and about 45 edits, so merging edits into the tick has almost nothing to merge. Proposed to the owner: skip R4, do R6 (presence at 10 Hz with pointers interpolated in the web app) next, R5 only if the remeasure asks. Waits for the owner's answer.

2026-10-13 performance 2: owner agreed to the new order: R4 (perf2-edit-batch) is not built, R6 goes next, R5 only if the remeasure asks. Slice perf2-presence-rate approved at G3 (PR 160). A room of 10 sockets or more sends presence at most once in 100 ms; the web app measures the gap between frames and moves pointers and dragged elements over 160 ms instead of 80, without knowing the rule. On a laptop, three rooms of 30: presence frames out 2270 to 1206 a second, the API container 21.4% to 18.5% of a core, the web container 12.1% to 9.2%, pointer p95 54 to 56 ms. Owner's decisions: the web app and the server ship in one release, not a release apart as the spec first said; no release yet. The threshold of 10 sockets is the agent's choice and has no ENV. Next: slice perf2-remeasure on DigitalOcean, ask the owner before spending.
